productive_patterns.description: Launch 3-5 agents in parallel for independent tasks (e.g., build 5 floor patterns simultaneously)
productive_patterns.when: Multiple artifacts or presets need building, each independent
productive_patterns.evidence: Built 10 floor patterns in one batch, 5 facade presets simultaneously
productive_patterns.caveat: Registry conflicts — agents may write to same JSON file. Commit after each completes.

productive_patterns.description: Build artifact → capture Godot screenshot → evaluate → fix → recapture
productive_patterns.when: Visual output needs to match a reference photo
productive_patterns.evidence: 14 meander iterations, each improving on the last
productive_patterns.effectiveness: High for visual matching, but requires clear reference
productive_patterns.caveat: Can loop forever if the reference is ambiguous. Set max iterations.

productive_patterns.description: Write a blog post ABOUT the problem to clarify thinking before solving it
productive_patterns.when: Stuck on a conceptual problem (not just a bug)
productive_patterns.evidence: Grid as Governance blog clarified the recursive grammar. QFEP blog defined the framework. Space-filling blog opened the ontological question.
productive_patterns.caveat: Takes time. Don't blog when you should be coding.

productive_patterns.description: Photograph in museum → analyze pattern → build procedural artifact → compare side-by-side
productive_patterns.when: Creating new patterns from real-world references
productive_patterns.evidence: 42 floor patterns from MANN and Pompeii photos
productive_patterns.effectiveness: High. The comparison reveals what the pattern IS (formal structure) vs what it ALSO IS (material, aging, context).
productive_patterns.caveat: The gap between photo and render is not failure — it IS the data (λ parameter).

productive_patterns.description: Build the 2D web editor first, iterate fast, THEN port to Godot 3D
productive_patterns.when: Building any new system (pattern maker, mosaic editor, facade builder, floor plan editor, meander editor)
productive_patterns.evidence: Every successful pipeline started in the web UI. The meander editor enabled drawing tiles that the GDScript couldn't get right alone.
productive_patterns.effectiveness: Essential. The web is where Claude thinks best. Godot is where the user experiences.
productive_patterns.caveat: The web→Godot JSON bridge can become a bottleneck if the format doesn't match.

productive_patterns.description: Alternate between building (practice) and writing (theory). Each informs the other.
productive_patterns.when: Always. This IS the research methodology.
productive_patterns.evidence: The meander iterations (practice) led to the space-filling ontology blog (theory) which reframed the problem as continuous vs discrete.
productive_patterns.effectiveness: This is what makes it RESEARCH, not just engineering.
productive_patterns.caveat: Don't get stuck in one mode. If you've been building for 2 hours, write. If you've been writing for 1 hour, build.

productive_patterns.description: Run heat_map_generator.py, pick the hottest actionable item, fix it, regenerate. The /continue skill automates this loop.
productive_patterns.when: Starting a session without a specific task, or finishing one task and looking for the next
productive_patterns.evidence: Heat map surfaces blocked items at 90, active topics at 60-80, empty sequences at 50. Fixes flow naturally.
productive_patterns.effectiveness: Eliminates 'what should I work on?' decision fatigue. Temperature = priority.
productive_patterns.caveat: Don't chase low-temperature items when high-temperature items exist. Fix blockers first.

productive_patterns.description: Solve the problem at a HIGHER abstraction level, then project the solution onto the implementation
productive_patterns.when: The implementation keeps failing (like the meander tile problem)
productive_patterns.evidence: Meander insight: define the braid topology FIRST, then project onto tiles. The tile system was the constraint, not the solution.
productive_patterns.effectiveness: Breakthrough pattern. If you're stuck, go UP one level.
productive_patterns.caveat: Requires recognizing WHEN you're fighting the wrong abstraction.

templates.name: Create a new floor pattern
steps: 1. Find/photograph reference image
2. Analyze: what are the repeating elements? what symmetry group?
3. Create .gd with class_name, ArrayMesh, MosaicPalette, StaticBody3D, apply_grid_config()
4. Create .tscn (minimal scene file)
5. Register in commons/artifacts/registry/arrays.json
6. Run Godot capture: capture_multi_angle.gd --mode=artifact --target=<name>
7. Copy captures to encyclopedia gallery + blog
8. Update capture-manifest.json
9. Place in a museum map for VR testing

templates.name: Create a new facade preset
steps: 1. Find/photograph reference building
2. Analyze: how many stories? bays? what zone hierarchy?
3. Create JSON in commons/facade_parts/presets/
4. Use version 3 format with zones, placements, materials
5. Test: point facade_builder.tscn to the new preset, capture
6. Compare to reference photo
7. Add to a museum map as exhibit_wall

templates.name: Create a new museum map
steps: 1. Design room layout on paper or in floor plan editor
2. Create floor_plan.json with rooms, doorways, open_edges
3. Assign floor_pattern and wall_preset to each room
4. Add exhibit_walls for freestanding facades
5. Create minimal map_data.json (structure + spawn + teleporter + floor_plan_space)
6. Verify: all rooms ≥5×5, corridors ≥3 wide, all reachable, facades fit
7. Register in sequence
8. Capture top-down screenshot

templates.name: Create a new web primitive editor
steps: 1. Identify the principle (what Godot infoboard does it match?)
2. Define the ONTOLOGICAL QUESTION (not 'how does it work' but 'what does it reveal?')
3. Build interactive canvas with the core concept
4. Add teaching content: 3 key lessons
5. Add JSON export for Godot bridge
6. Add to /primitives index page
7. Write the lens description for PRIMITIVE_ONTOLOGY.md

templates.name: Deep investigation of a pattern/concept
steps: 1. Start with the reference photo or concept
2. Try the simplest implementation
3. Capture, compare, identify what's wrong
4. Try a different approach
5. Document EACH iteration (screenshot + description)
6. After 3-5 iterations, STOP and write about what you learned
7. If stuck, go UP one abstraction level
8. Blog the investigation (the failures ARE the research)
9. Record discoveries in LOD_DISCOVERIES.json

directions_to_explore.description: Solve the meander with continuous coordinates, not tiles. The boundary function works — the rendering needs per-stone freedom.
directions_to_explore.theoretical_connection: This connects to the question of discrete vs continuous, which connects to Cantor's continuum, which connects to the ontology of space.

directions_to_explore.description: Build web editors for all 20 infoboard principles. 3 done, 17 to go.
directions_to_explore.theoretical_connection: Each primitive is a LENS on reality. The collection of lenses IS a theory of computation.

directions_to_explore.description: Build the aedicula_frame part — the temple-front frame that defines Fourth Style wall painting. Missing from part catalog.
directions_to_explore.theoretical_connection: The aedicula is the FRAME — it declares that what's inside has been lifted into the space of representation. It's a visual bracket, a border, a reading protocol.

directions_to_explore.description: Fix the floor plan space y_offset so museum floors align with the grid system floor. Currently broken — floors float or sink.
directions_to_explore.theoretical_connection: The gap between the platform you stand on and the museum you see is a literal λ parameter — the distance between system and content.

directions_to_explore.description: Place science_screen artifacts in museum maps next to the floor patterns they abstract. The 2D mirror next to the 3D reality.
directions_to_explore.theoretical_connection: The gap between 3D experience and 2D representation IS the research question made visible.

anti-patterns.description: Don't start with the tile/implementation. Start with the RULE/TOPOLOGY, then project down.
anti-patterns.learned_from: 14 meander iterations — every tile-first approach produced identical repeated hooks

anti-patterns.description: 22 museum maps but most haven't been tested in VR. Quality over quantity.
anti-patterns.learned_from: Building maps is fast but verifying they work in VR is slow and we skip it

anti-patterns.description: Adding jitter to tiles doesn't make them mosaics. The DECISION must be free, not just the rendering.
anti-patterns.learned_from: Meander v14: jittered positions but grid-snapped decisions. Looked identical to v13.
